We need to return the pair with smallest i, then smallest j. Using a hash map approach: iterate j, check if target - xs[j] seen before. But that gives smallest j first, and for that j the largest i (if we overwrite). We need smallest i then smallest j.

To get smallest i first: for each i, find if there's a j > i with xs[i]+xs[j]==target, choosing smallest such j. Brute force O(n^2) works but we can do better.

Approach: iterate i from 0; for each i, we need smallest j>i with xs[j] == target - xs[i]. Precompute for each value, sorted list of indices. Then for each i in order, binary search in the list of indices for target-xs[i] for the smallest index > i. First i that yields a match gives answer. That's O(n log n).

Simpler: build dict value -> sorted list of indices. Then loop i ascending, bisect for index > i. Return (i, j) at first found.

Handle empty input: return None.

Use bisect from standard library (allowed).
